cards.prose: *When ye stand praying, forgive*, he says, and Leviticus has the same command in the commandment itself: *Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge*, and *thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself*. Forgiving at the hour of prayer is that Torah kept, the grudge let go as the man asks to be forgiven.
cards.member_sentence: Leviticus forbids vengeance and grudges against the children of thy people and commands love for the neighbour as thyself.

cards.prose: Matthew puts this right beneath the pattern of prayer: *if ye forgive men their trespasses*, the heavenly Father will forgive too. Mark sets it at the end of the word on prayer after the fig tree, as the thing to do *when ye stand praying*, with *if ye have ought against any* spoken to the man already on his feet before the Father.
cards.member_sentence: Matthew says if you forgive men their trespasses your heavenly Father will also forgive you.

cards.prose: At Caesarea Philippi Yahusha (Jesus) asked *Whom do men say that I the Son of Adam am?* and got only what men guessed. In the temple *the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders* ask by what authority he does these things, and when he asks about John's baptism they will not say whether it was from heaven.
cards.member_sentence: Matthew has Yahusha (Jesus) ask what men say of him, the same ground of who he is and by whose authority he acts.
cards.flag: The pair is loose: the link is the question of who he is and the guesses men make (John), not a stated parallel.

cards.prose: Mark names three groups, *the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders*, where Matthew names *the chief priests and the elders of the people*, and Mark has him *walking in the temple* where Matthew has him teaching. The question is the same, and so is his answer about John's baptism.
cards.member_phrase: the chief priests and the elders of the people came unto him as he was teaching
cards.member_sentence: Matthew has the chief priests and elders of the people come to him as he teaches in the temple with the same question.
